definition: A bigram or digram is a sequence of two adjacent elements from a string of tokens, which are typically letters, syllables, or words.
details: A bigram is an n-gram for n=2. The frequency distribution of every bigram in a string is commonly used for simple statistical analysis of text in many applications, including in computational linguistics, cryptography, and speech recognition. Gappy bigrams or skipping bigrams are word pairs which allow gaps (perhaps avoiding connecting words, or allowing some simulation of dependencies, as in a dependency grammar).
story: Think of a historian sorting through boxes of letters, building a picture of an era one sentence at a time. Every machine is shaped by what it was shown, so someone has to choose that material with care. The examples a machine reads become the world it believes in. The words a model reads become the world it believes in. And that is Bigram — the unglamorous work everything else stands on.
